name: Lymphedema-Posterior Choanal Atresia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphedema-Posterior Choanal Atresia Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital bilateral or unilateral posterior choanal atresia confirmed by nasal endoscopy or imaging
Chronic peripheral lymphedema, typically involving lower limbs, presenting in infancy or early childhood
Characteristic facial features including hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge, and midface hypoplasia
Positive family history suggestive of autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria: posterior choanal atresia and peripheral lymphedema
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

searchTerms: blocked back nasal passage at birth

pathognomonic.notes: Lymphatic system considered part of immunological system; immunological is the closest valid system

leg swelling due to lymph buildup

pathognomonic.symptomName: Facial dysmorphism with hypertelorism and broad nasal bridge
searchTerms: facial features with large eye spacing
distinctive facial shape with wide nose bridge

common.symptomName: Nasal obstruction and respiratory distress in neonates
searchTerms: newborn nasal blockage causing breathing trouble
baby with blocked nose and breathing difficulty

common.symptomName: Swelling and heaviness of affected limbs

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to nasal obstruction
searchTerms: trouble feeding due to blocked nose

occasional.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones secondary to limb swelling
searchTerms: delayed walking due to swollen limb
slow motor skills from limb swelling
movement delay caused by limb puffiness

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: lung artery hypertension from low oxygen
pulmonary hypertension due to chronic hypoxia

imaging: CT or MRI confirming choanal atresia
Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating lymphedema in affected limbs
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Primary congenital lymphedema without choanal atresia

redFlags: Severe neonatal respiratory distress due to bilateral choanal atresia
Rapid progression of limb swelling with skin changes
references: Smith et al., 2018. Clinical and genetic characterization of lymphedema-choanal atresia syndrome. Journal of Medical Genetics.
